key_insight: A parametric PINN and a tensorial reduced-order model can both learn a direct space-time-to-state map for shallow-water dam-break flows without time integration, but the PINN needs shock-aware collocation to remain robust near discontinuities.
engineering_relevance: The study offers two fast surrogate modeling options for parametric CFD-style flood/wave problems, supporting rapid prediction across unseen dam-break conditions.
method: Parametric PINN: learns the solution map from space, time, and dam-break parameters to the flow state.
Tensorial reduced-order model (TROM): non-intrusive surrogate that also maps inputs directly to the physical state.
Comparison focuses on out-of-sample and extrapolated parameter values, with special treatment for shock regions in the PINN.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a detailed comparison on out-of-sample and extrapolated parameters and highlights improved robustness when shock-aware collocation is added to the PINN.
watch_item: Both surrogates are tested on a 1D shallow-water dam-break case, so generalization to more complex multi-dimensional flows and stronger shocks may require additional validation.
paper_title: Comparison of a Parametric Physics-Informed Neural Network and a Tensorial Reduced-Order Model for the Shallow-Water Dam-Break Problem
